lessons.title: Indices and surds
lessons.programRef: Cameroon GCE Board — Advanced Level Mathematics, Pure Mathematics (to be checked against the official syllabus)

lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use the laws of indices with integer and fractional powers
reviewNotes: Scope of surds/indices in the GCE Board syllabus (fractional and negative powers assumed standard) to be confirmed.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Laws of indices
blocks.md: For $a>0$: $a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}$, $a^m \div a^n = a^{m-n}$, $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$, $a^0 = 1$, $a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}$. Fractional powers are roots: $a^{1/n} = \sqrt[n]{a}$ and $a^{m/n} = (\sqrt[n]{a})^m$.

blocks.title: Surds
blocks.md: A surd is an irrational root such as $\sqrt{2}$. Rules: $\sqrt{a}\sqrt{b} = \sqrt{ab}$ and $\sqrt{a/b} = \sqrt{a}/\sqrt{b}$. Simplify by taking out square factors: $\sqrt{72} = \sqrt{36 \times 2} = 6\sqrt{2}$.

blocks.caption: Graphs of $y=2^x$ (growth) and $y=(1/2)^x$ (decay) both pass through $(0,1)$ because $a^0=1$.
blocks.alt: Two exponential curves crossing the y-axis at 1, one rising and one falling.

blocks.title: Rationalising the denominator
blocks.md: To remove a surd from a denominator multiply top and bottom by the **conjugate**. The conjugate of $a + \sqrt{b}$ is $a - \sqrt{b}$, and $(a+\sqrt{b})(a-\sqrt{b}) = a^2 - b$ is rational.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- $(a+b)^2 \neq a^2 + b^2$: there is a middle term $2ab$.
- $\sqrt{a+b} \neq \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}$.
- $2^{-3}$ is $\frac{1}{8}$, not $-8$.
- $\sqrt{x^2} = |x|$, not simply $x$.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate $3+\sqrt{3}$.

objectives: Convert between index and logarithm form
Solve equations of the form $a^x = b$
reviewNotes: Natural logarithm (ln) is assumed known from this lesson; the exponential function itself is treated in the 'Exponential and logarithmic functions' lesson.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Definition and laws
blocks.md: $\log_a x = y$ means $a^y = x$ (with $a>0$, $a\neq1$, $x>0$). Laws: $\log_a(xy)=\log_a x+\log_a y$, $\log_a\frac{x}{y}=\log_a x-\log_a y$, $\log_a x^k = k\log_a x$. Also $\log_a a=1$ and $\log_a 1=0$.

blocks.title: Solving $a^x = b$
blocks.md: Take logarithms of both sides (base 10 or $\ln$): $x\log a = \log b$, so $x = \frac{\log b}{\log a}$. The change of base formula is $\log_a b = \frac{\log b}{\log a}$.

blocks.caption: The graph of $y=\log_2 x$: it passes through $(1,0)$, $(2,1)$, $(8,3)$ and is undefined for $x\leq0$.
blocks.alt: Increasing logarithm curve through (1,0), (2,1) and (8,3) with the y-axis as a vertical asymptote.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- $\log(a+b)$ is NOT $\log a + \log b$.
- $\frac{\log a}{\log b}$ is NOT $\log a - \log b$.
- In equations with logs, check every answer: the argument of a log must stay positive, so some roots must be rejected.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps: The arguments must be positive: $x>3$. So $x=-5$ is rejected.

lessons.title: Quadratic functions and equations
lessons.programRef: Cameroon GCE Board — Advanced Level Mathematics, Pure Mathematics (to be checked against the official syllabus)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Complete the square and find the turning point
Use the discriminant to describe the roots
Use sum and product of roots
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Completing the square
blocks.md: $ax^2+bx+c = a\left(x+\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + c-\frac{b^2}{4a}$. The parabola has its turning point at $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$, a minimum if $a>0$ and a maximum if $a<0$.

blocks.title: Discriminant
blocks.md: For $ax^2+bx+c=0$ the discriminant is $\Delta=b^2-4ac$. If $\Delta>0$: two distinct real roots; $\Delta=0$: one repeated root; $\Delta<0$: no real roots. Roots: $x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{\Delta}}{2a}$.

blocks.title: Sum and product of roots
blocks.md: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $ax^2+bx+c=0$ then $\alpha+\beta=-\frac{b}{a}$ and $\alpha\beta=\frac{c}{a}$. These let you build a new equation from given roots.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.md: Equal roots means $\Delta=0$ exactly. Always move everything to one side ($=0$) before reading off $a$, $b$, $c$. Divide by $a$ BEFORE completing the square.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Write $x^2-6x+4$ in the form $(x-p)^2+q$ and state the minimum value.
steps: A square is at least 0, so the minimum is $-5$, at $x=3$.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Find the values of $k$ for which $x^2+kx+9=0$ has equal roots.

objectives: Solve simple modulus equations and inequalities
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Quadratic inequalities
blocks.md: Find the roots of the related equation, sketch the parabola, then read the answer. For $ax^2+bx+c>0$ with $a>0$: outside the roots; for $<0$: between the roots. Write answers like $x<-2$ or $x>3$.

blocks.title: Modulus
blocks.md: $|x|=x$ if $x\geq0$ and $|x|=-x$ if $x<0$; it is the distance from 0. $|x-a|<r$ means $a-r<x<a+r$; $|x-a|>r$ means $x<a-r$ or $x>a+r$.

blocks.caption: Number line for $-2<x<3$: open circles at the ends are not included.
blocks.alt: Number line from -4 to 5 with open circles at -2 and 3 and the segment between them shaded.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Multiplying or dividing by a NEGATIVE number reverses the inequality sign.
- Never square-root or divide by $x$ without checking its sign.
- $|x|=a$ has two solutions for $a>0$; check each against the original equation.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps: The parabola opens upwards, so it is positive outside the roots.

lessons.title: Polynomials: factor and remainder theorems
lessons.programRef: Cameroon GCE Board — Advanced Level Mathematics, Pure Mathematics (to be checked against the official syllabus)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use the remainder and factor theorems
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Remainder theorem
blocks.md: When a polynomial $f(x)$ is divided by $(x-a)$ the remainder is $f(a)$. For $(ax-b)$ the remainder is $f\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)$.

blocks.title: Factor theorem
blocks.md: $(x-a)$ is a factor of $f(x)$ if and only if $f(a)=0$. Then $a$ is a root of $f(x)=0$ and the graph crosses the x-axis at $x=a$.

blocks.title: Factorising a cubic
blocks.md:
1. Try $x=\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,s'$ (factors of the constant term) until $f(a)=0$.
2. Divide $f(x)$ by $(x-a)$ (long division or inspection) to get a quadratic.
3. Factorise the quadratic.
4. List all roots.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md: A factor $(x+3)$ corresponds to the root $x=-3$, not $+3$. Remember the sign: test $f(-3)$ for the factor $(x+3)$.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Find the remainder when $2x^3+x^2-3x+5$ is divided by $(x+2)$.

lessons.title: Functions: composite and inverse

objectives: Find inverse functions and relate their graphs
reviewNotes: Check whether the syllabus asks for one-to-one/many-to-one terminology and graph transformations (translations, stretches); transformations of graphs are not covered in this pack.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Function, domain, range
blocks.md: A function $f$ gives exactly one output for each input. The **domain** is the set of allowed inputs, the **range** the set of outputs. Examples: $\sqrt{x-3}$ needs $x\geq3$; $\frac{1}{x-5}$ needs $x\neq5$.

blocks.title: Composite function
blocks.md: $fg(x)=f(g(x))$: apply $g$ first, then $f$. In general $fg\neq gf$. Work from the inside out.

blocks.title: Finding an inverse
blocks.md: Write $y=f(x)$, make $x$ the subject, then swap letters: $f^{-1}(x)$. The graph of $y=f^{-1}(x)$ is the reflection of $y=f(x)$ in the line $y=x$. Only one-to-one functions have an inverse; restrict the domain if needed. The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md: $f^{-1}(x)$ is NOT $\frac{1}{f(x)}$. For $fg(x)$ do $g$ first. A function like $x^2$ has no inverse on all of $\mathbb{R}$ because two inputs give one output.
